title: Dense affine immersion in a finite-type algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], put $B=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with a specified map to $S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $f:X\to B$ be separated of finite type [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. There exist a quasi-compact open subspace $U\subseteq X$, dense in the atlas point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology], an integer $n\geq0$, and an immersion $a:U\to\mathbf A^n_B$ over $B$ [def-nagata-relative-affine-space]. Here an open subspace is represented on every scheme test by an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and an immersion is represented on every scheme test by a closed immersion followed by an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. In particular $U$ is a scheme. The space $X$ and the base ring need not be reduced, and $X$ need not be irreducible or flat over $B$.

source.place: Tag 088N (lemma-embedding-into-affine-over-qs), specialized to a separated finite-type space over an affine Noetherian scheme. Finite presentation and Noetherianity used in this specialization are spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 06G4 (lemma-noetherian-finite-type-finite-presentation), 04ZK (lemma-locally-finite-type-locally-noetherian), and 04ZL (lemma-finite-presentation-noetherian).

proof.text: The scheme morphism $B\to S$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]. By the Yoneda identification $h_B\times_{h_S}h_B=h_{B\times_SB}$, the diagonal of $h_B\to h_S$ is represented by the scheme diagonal $B\to B\times_SB$, a closed immersion; its pullback along any scheme $T\to B\times_SB$ is the scheme fibre product $B\times_{B\times_SB}T\to T$, a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. So $B\to S$ is separated as a morphism of algebraic spaces. The given $f$ is separated. By [lem-sfb-space-quasiseparated-test-calculus], both morphisms are quasi-separated and their composite $X\to S$ is quasi-separated, i.e. $\Delta:X\to X\times_SX$ is quasi-compact. For a scheme $T\to X\times_SX$ the pullback $P=X\times_{X\times_SX}T$ is a scheme (the diagonal of an algebraic space is representable), and for a quasi-compact open $W\subseteq T$ the open $P\times_TW$ is a quasi-compact algebraic space, i.e. receives a surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme; its image is all of $P\times_TW$, which is therefore quasi-compact. Thus the diagonal satisfies the scheme-test hypothesis of [lem-sfb-quasiseparated-space-dense-scheme-open]. Apply that node to obtain an open immersion $j:V\to X$ with $V$ a scheme and $|V|$ open dense in $|X|$.

source.place: Tag 088N, lemma-embedding-into-affine-over-qs, first paragraph: pass to a dense open scheme; relative quasi-separatedness is sufficient.

proof.text: The affine scheme $B=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is locally Noetherian by the one-member affine covering in [pqf-def-locnoeth], and is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Finite type in [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] includes quasi-compactness; testing $f$ on the affine target $B$ gives quasi-compactness of $X$. For every etale scheme chart $T\to X$, the chart test for $f$, with target chart $\mathrm{id}_B$, says that $T\to B$ is locally of finite type. Thus [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes every such $T$ locally Noetherian. This is precisely local Noetherianity on etale charts. Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-topology] to conclude that $|X|$ is Noetherian. Hence its open subspace $|V|$ is Noetherian: an increasing chain of opens of $V$ is an increasing chain of opens of $X$, since $V$ is open.

source.place: Tag 04ZK, lemma-locally-finite-type-locally-noetherian; spaces-properties.tex lemma-Noetherian-topology, and Tag 088N first paragraph.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components] and [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], write $|V|=C_1\cup\cdots\cup C_r$ as its finitely many distinct irreducible components. Put $O_i=V\setminus\bigcup_{k\ne i}C_k$. This is open, contained in $C_i$, and nonempty: otherwise the irreducible set $C_i$ would be contained in a finite union of other components and hence in one of them, contradicting maximality and distinctness. The elementary finite-union assertion follows by induction from the definition of irreducibility. Pick $x_i\in O_i$ and use [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] to choose an affine open $W_i$ with $x_i\in W_i\subseteq O_i$. The $W_i$ are pairwise disjoint. Each nonempty open $W_i$ of the irreducible space $C_i$ is dense in $C_i$: it meets every other nonempty open by irreducibility. Thus $U=\bigcup_iW_i$ is open dense in $V$ and consequently in $X$. If $V$ is empty take $r=0$ and $U=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 088N, lemma-embedding-into-affine-over-qs, first paragraph: remove component intersections and shrink each remaining irreducible open to an affine; no reducedness assumption.

proof.text: Write $W_i\simeq\operatorname{Spec}R_i$. The open subscheme $U$ with its restricted structure sheaf is the coproduct of the $W_i$: a morphism out of $U$ is exactly a family of morphisms out of its disjoint open pieces, glued uniquely on their empty overlaps. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum] to identify $U\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_iR_i)$. In particular $U$ is affine and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. The inclusions $U\subseteq V\subseteq X$ give an open subspace of $X$, because after any scheme test they are successive inclusions of open subschemes with restricted structure sheaves. The empty product is the zero ring, so this also covers $X=\varnothing$.

source.place: lemma-disjoint-union-affines; its finite iteration, equivalently the finite coproduct-spectrum isomorphism.

proof.text: The open immersion $U\to X$ is representable etale: on each scheme test it is an open immersion, which is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. Apply the chart definition [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] to $U\to X$, $\mathrm{id}_B:B\to B$ and $f|_U:U\to B$. It gives local finite type of this scheme morphism. Both $U$ and $B$ are affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes $U\to B$ quasi-compact. Therefore $U\to B$ is of finite type. The first conclusion of [lem-chow-affine-immersion] now gives an integer $n\geq0$ and a closed immersion $U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_B$ over $B$, hence the requested immersion (take the open factor to be the identity). This uses the full structure sheaves of the chosen opens throughout; it takes no reduction and assumes neither irreducibility nor flatness of $X$.
